page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is a burstable, entry-level virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.t6-c1m2.large delivers entry-tier performance across compute and memory subsystems. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core CPU score of 1300.19 and a multi-core score of 2402.69, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 186.46 GB/sec, but this drops significantly to 20.68 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, placing it in the bottom 10%. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the performance constraints of its burstable CPU allocation model.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its burstable CPU allocation and lack of local storage, which limits its capability under sustained heavy workloads. It is designed for low-intensity, intermittent tasks where resource consumption spikes occasionally but remains low on average. Qualitative cost efficiency is high for lightweight environments due to its minimal resource footprint. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, lightweight database operations, small-scale text processing, and development or testing environments that do not require continuous high-performance compute.
